messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: High p95/p99 latency observed for /v1/generate (continuous-batching runtime). Rate of long-seq requests spiked ~3x at 10:02 UTC. Paging oncall.

jamie_oncall: Acked. I'm on it. grabbing logs + tracing now. anyone able to confirm customer impact? :eyes:

marc_sre: I'm seeing backlog growth on batcher workers, GC spikes on a subset of pods. Continuous batching windows are accumulating >2500 pending tokens. p95 up to 900ms, p99 up to 2.4s. Throughput nominal but latency tail is bad.

ria_eng_infra: adding - looks like `continuous_batching.max_window_ms` is 80ms at current config and `max_batch_tokens` = 4096. We can lower window to reduce tail at cost of throughput. Also we can set `continuous_batching.enabled=false` to fall back to fixed batching.

jamie_oncall: Good options. Priority: reduce customer-impact > keep throughput. Proposed mitigations (in order):
1) Apply per-route short-term rate limit to 50 req/s for the top noisy route for 10m.
2) Lower `max_window_ms` to 20ms and `max_batch_tokens` to 2048.
3) If still bad, disable continuous batching on affected pool and force small fixed batches.
4) Throttle one high-volume customer if they match signature.

marc_sre: Agreed. I'll push config 1 & 2 now to canary then rollout.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: config/continuous-batching/2026-03-15-1 -> pool:batchers-canary (3 pods)

marc_sre: (code)
```
# apply short-term per-route quota
redwoodctl rate-limit set --route "/v1/generate" --limit 50 --window 60 --ttl 600
# update batching config
redwoodctl config set continuous_batching.max_window_ms=20
redwoodctl config set continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens=2048
```

tess_prod: Notifying customers now. I'll open a CS thread and flag customers using long-seq preview endpoints. cs-lead tagging.

cs-lead: Thanks — we'll message the top 5 customers and offer temporary quota bump after mitigation if they see regressions.

ria_eng_infra: Canary metrics: p95 dropped from 900ms -> 260ms, p99 -> 620ms on canary. Backlog reduced by ~70%.

jamie_oncall: Rollout to remaining batcher pool in 3m, monitor 10m. Oncall handoff at +30m if stable.

marc_sre: Rolling out to prod pools now. deploy-bot will emit final status.

deploy-bot: rollout finished: config/continuous-batching/2026-03-15-1 -> pool:batchers-prod (12 pods) :white_check_mark:

jamie_oncall: Observability: set alert threshold lowered to p99 > 1.5s, trace sampling increased for /v1/generate for 15m. Also snapshot KV cache hit rates.

marc_sre: Noted. Also created a short-lived traffic-shaper rule to prioritize low-latency routes:
```
redwoodctl traffic-shape create --name small-req-priority --match 'tokens<=512' --priority high --ttl 900
```

tess_prod: Customer update sent. Affected customers acknowledged; one asked to be throttled temporarily to help aggregate stability.

jamie_oncall: Good. We'll keep continuous batching enabled but with tuned params. Next steps: 1) run load test replay at 3am with new settings; 2) open follow-up ticket to analyze outlier requests > 2k tokens; 3) consider adaptive windowing experiment.

marc_sre: Handing off to ria for next 30m oncall follow-through. I'm available if things spike back up.

ria_eng_infra: Taking it. I'll watch the dashboard and keep the throttle window ready. If p99 climbs >1.2s I'll start disabling continuous batching on the noisy pool and notify.

jamie_oncall: Thanks team. Final note: document the exact config blob in the incident tracker and tag for postmortem if we hit customer SLA breach. :thumbsup:

ria_eng_infra: logging configs to incident ticket 6421. handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
